evidence_text: Goodwill is a special type of intangible asset. Goodwill and intangible assets are usually listed as separate items

Goodwill represents that portion of the entire business value that cannot be attributed to other income producing business assets, tangible or intangible. Goodwill is a special type of intangible asset.
Anybody buying that company would book $10 million in total assets acquired... Any consideration paid in excess of $10 million shall be considered as goodwill.
Any consideration paid in excess of $10 million shall be considered as goodwill. Its magnitude depends on the two other variables by definition.
logical_form: if goodwill is calculated then its magnitude depends on other variables
mechanism: The calculation of goodwill's value determines its magnitude.

evidence_text: In a private company, goodwill has no predetermined value prior to the acquisition. A publicly traded company is subject to a constant process of market valuation, so goodwill will always be apparent.

evidence_text: The accounting treatment for goodwill remains controversial... This creates a mismatch between the reported assets and net incomes of companies that have grown without purchasing other companies, and those that have.
logical_form: if goodwill accounting is controversial then it creates a mismatch
mechanism: The controversial accounting treatment of goodwill leads to inconsistencies in reported assets and net incomes.

evidence_text: This creates a mismatch... while companies will follow the rules prescribed by the Accounting Standards Boards, there is not a fundamentally correct way to deal with this mismatch under the current financial reporting framework.
logical_form: if there is a mismatch then there is not a fundamentally correct way to deal with it
mechanism: The mismatch in reported assets and net incomes makes it difficult to find a fundamentally correct way to deal with it under the current financial reporting framework.

evidence_text: The accounting for goodwill will be rules based. Those rules have changed, and can be expected to continue to change, periodically along with the changes in the members of the Accounting Standards Boards.
logical_form: if accounting for goodwill is rules based then the rules will change
mechanism: The rules-based nature of goodwill accounting makes it subject to changes based on the decisions of the Accounting Standards Boards.

evidence_text: Those rules have changed... The current rules governing the accounting treatment of goodwill are highly subjective and can result in very high costs, but have limited value to investors.
logical_form: if the rules change then the current rules are subjective
mechanism: Changes in rules can lead to the current rules being subjective and costly.
